title: Teaching procedures run as rulesets
statement: Whether a lesson that adapts at each student action within written rulesets, for reading sequences and for procedures such as comparative judgement and faded non-examples, helps readers is untested.
example: Of three procedures planned as rulesets, two already have a block and the faded non-example has none.
detail: A planned stage of the lesson engine would run procedures as rulesets, among them full modelling, comparative judgement and faded non-examples, and reading sequences from first-read checks through close reading and analysis to writing, with the judge deciding sequencing, hints and escalation at each action within those rules (`g9/transformer/v05/README.md`). Its exit criterion is sequencing measured with scripted readers before any student sees it. Today a worked-model block and a compare-two-answers block exist, no faded non-example does (`g9/transformer/v04/README.md`), and none of it runs as a ruleset.

evidence.quote: - Adaptive sequencing, hints and escalation, decided by Jev at each action within rules.
Procedures as rulesets: full teacher modelling, comparative judgement and faded non-examples
reading sequences (first-read checks, close reading, analysis, writing)
- **Judge:** compare two answers ✓, faded non-example, rank the evidence.
follows a quotation unpicked, rebuilds one sentence, then reads the model paragraph
**Exit criteria:** sequencing measured with personas before any student sees it.
